title: Ordinary Hecke Specht Polytabloids and Signed Murphy Comparison

items.title: Hecke row permutation modules and ordinary Dipper-James polytabloids
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$, $n\ge0$, and let $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ be the type-A Hecke algebra with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, relations $(T_i-q)(T_i+1)=0$, braid and distant commutation, standard basis $\{T_w\}$ and star anti-involution $T_i^*=T_i$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). All modules are right modules. Write $t\cdot\sigma$ for the right action of $S_n$ on tableaux defined by $(t\cdot\sigma)(c):=\sigma^{-1}(t(c))$; it is the inverse of the left action of [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]].

For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$ let $S_\lambda$ be its row (Young) subgroup, let $t^\lambda$ be the row-filled $\lambda$-tableau, let $t_\lambda$ be the column-filled $\lambda$-tableau, let $D_\lambda=\{d\in S_n:t^\lambda\cdot d\text{ is row standard}\}$ be the set of minimal-length right coset representatives, and let $w_\lambda\in S_n$ be the unique element with $t^\lambda\cdot w_\lambda=t_\lambda$. Put
$$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w,\qquad y_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}(-q)^{-\ell(w)}T_w,\qquad z_\lambda:=x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}y_{\lambda'},$$
where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). The **row permutation module** is the right ideal $M(\lambda):=x_\lambda H\subseteq H$, and the **ordinary Dipper-James polytabloid module** is $P(\lambda):=z_\lambda H\subseteq M(\lambda)$; $z_\lambda$ is its polytabloid generator.

The **permutation form** is the $R$-bilinear form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ defined on the distinguished family $\{x_\lambda T_d:d\in D_\lambda\}$ by $\beta(x_\lambda T_d,x_\lambda T_e)=\delta_{d,e}q^{\ell(d)}$; the **DJ form** is its restriction to $P(\lambda)$. For $\lambda=\varnothing$ set $x_\varnothing=y_\varnothing=z_\varnothing=1$, so that $M(\varnothing)=P(\varnothing)=R$ and $\beta$ is the standard form. Every base change $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto q$, produces all objects over $R$ by the same formulas; the suppliers below prove that the distinguished families and the form are base-change compatible. Empty shapes and the cases $n=0,1$ are included. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: A definition item that fixes the normalizations; the mathematical structure is supplied by the later items of this page. The elements $x_\lambda,y_\lambda,w_\lambda$ and the modules $M(\lambda),P(\lambda)$ are the Dipper-James conventions exactly as indexed in Fayers, 'An algorithm for semistandardising homomorphisms' (author version), §2.1: $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in W_\lambda}T_w$, $y_\lambda=\sum_{w\in W_\lambda}(-q)^{-\ell(w)}T_w$, $w_\lambda$ determined by $t^\lambda w_\lambda=t_\lambda$, $M^\lambda=x_\lambda H_n$, $S^\lambda=x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}y_{\lambda'}H_n$. Fayers's field hypothesis and parameter name are immaterial: the formulas are polynomial and define the objects after every base change in which $q$ is invertible. The dictionary between Fayers's right tableau action $t\mapsto tw$ and the library's left action $\sigma\cdot t$ is $t\cdot\sigma=\sigma^{-1}\cdot t$, and under it $D_\lambda$ and $w_\lambda$ agree. Heard-Kujawa, arXiv:2207.00654, §2.2-§2.5, carries the same combinatorial generator $z_\lambda=x_\lambda T_{\sigma_\lambda}y_{\lambda^{\mathsf T}}$ (their $\sigma_\lambda$ is this $w_\lambda$) and the same standard-basis indexing by standard tableaux of the transposed shape (their (2.5.1), which quotes the Dipper-James basis theorem [DJ86, Theorem 5.6]). Their Hecke normalization is the symmetric one $(T_i-q)(T_i+q^{-1})=0$ with $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}q^{\ell(w)}T_w$, so HK supply the combinatorial shape of the construction, not the exact coefficients, which are fixed here in the $(T_i-q)(T_i+1)=0$ normalization. Definitional scope: the permutation form is fixed here by its values on the distinguished free family proved in [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]]; it is a chosen contravariant form and the historical DJ self-form on $S^\lambda$ is its restriction, not an additional source claim. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The row permutation module: distinguished basis and Hecke action
items.statement:
In the notation of [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], for every commutative $R$ and every $q\in R^\times$:

1. $M(\lambda)$ is free with basis $\{x_\lambda T_d:d\in D_\lambda\}$;
2. $x_\lambda T_w=q^{\ell(w)}x_\lambda$ and $T_wx_\lambda=q^{\ell(w)}x_\lambda$ for every $w\in S_\lambda$, and $x_\lambda^*=x_\lambda$;
3. if $d\in D_\lambda$, $t=t^\lambda\cdot d$ and $s=t\cdot s_i=t^\lambda\cdot d'$, then
$$x_\lambda T_dT_i=\begin{cases}q\,x_\lambda T_d,&s\text{ is not row standard},\\ x_\lambda T_{d'},&s\text{ is row standard and }\ell(d')>\ell(d),\\ q\,x_\lambda T_{d'}+(q-1)x_\lambda T_d,&s\text{ is row standard and }\ell(d')<\ell(d);\end{cases}$$
4. the basis and the action formulas are compatible with every base change $R\to R'$ along a ring map sending $q$ to a unit.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Direct transcription of the standard row-module facts from the two independent treatments read for this page. Mathas, manuscript, §3: Lemma 3.2 gives $m_\lambda T_w=q^{\ell(w)}m_\lambda$ for $w\in S_\lambda$; Proposition 3.3 gives that $D_\lambda$ is a set of right coset representatives with $\ell(wd)=\ell(w)+\ell(d)$ for $w\in S_\lambda$, $d\in D_\lambda$; Corollary 3.4 shows that $M_\lambda$ is free on the family $m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ and proves exactly the three-case formula displayed in (3). Ryom-Hansen, arXiv:0904.4243v5, §2, equations (5)-(6), states the same basis and the same action rules for $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ in the same normalization. The left identities in (2) follow from the right ones by $x_\lambda^*=x_\lambda$ and $\ell(w^{-1})=\ell(w)$. Part (4) is immediate because all structure constants are Laurent polynomials in $q$. The verification of (3) in the sources is the coset bookkeeping of Mathas §3. This item does not assert the cell law or the polytabloid basis; those are separate suppliers on this page. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Hecke sign automorphism, pullback and contragredient dual
items.statement:
For every commutative $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive $R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with $\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.
2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying $R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$ is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.
3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with $(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.
4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit $q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
(1) Since $T_i^{-1}=q^{-1}T_i+(q^{-1}-1)$, one has $-qT_i^{-1}=(q-1)-T_i$; the assignment $T_i\mapsto(q-1)-T_i$ exchanges the two roots $q$ and $-1$ of the quadratic relation and preserves the braid and distant-commutation relations, so it defines an algebra endomorphism; $\theta^2$ fixes every generator, hence $\theta^2=\mathrm{id}$. For a reduced word, $\theta(T_w)=\prod_j((q-1)-T_{i_j})=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{i_1}^{-1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}^{-1}=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$. Since $*$ fixes each $T_i$ and $\theta$ is built from the generators, $\theta$ commutes with $*$. Base change is immediate from the formulas.

(2) Functoriality of pullback along an involutive automorphism is formal; exactness of $(-)^\theta$ is exactness of the identity functor with a twisted action, and submodules, quotients, composition multiplicities and simplicity are unchanged because the underlying lattices and inclusion relations are unchanged.

(3) $(f\cdot h)(m)=f(mh^*)$ is a right action because $**=\mathrm{id}$; for finite free $M$ the dual basis computes the rank and all assertions are preserved by base change. The equality $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$ is the computation $(f\cdot h)(m)=f(m\theta(h^*))=(f\theta(h))(m)$, using that $\theta$ commutes with $*$.

(4) It suffices to prove $\theta(x_{(m)})=q^{\binom m2}y_{(m)}$ for one row: the row subgroup $S_\lambda$ is a direct product of symmetric groups on disjoint intervals, the corresponding $x$- and $y$-elements multiply, and $\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}{2}=\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))$. Work over the fraction field $K=\mathbb Q(q)$ of $A=\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$, where $H_K$ is split semisimple (Hoefsmit's theorem; Mathas, manuscript, Corollary 3.22 (Hoefsmit), printed p. 26). Since $T_ix_{(m)}=qx_{(m)}$ by [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]], one computes $T_i\theta(x_{(m)})=\theta(\theta(T_i)x_{(m)})=\theta(((q-1)-T_i)x_{(m)})=\theta(-x_{(m)})=-\theta(x_{(m)})$; hence $\theta(x_{(m)})$ lies in the space of vectors killed by all $T_i+1$, which is the sign isotypic component of the left regular representation of the split semisimple $H_K$ and is one-dimensional, spanned by the nonzero element $y_{(m)}$. So $\theta(x_{(m)})=cy_{(m)}$ for some $c\in K^\times$. Apply the algebra character $\rho_-:H_K\to K$, $T_i\mapsto-1$ (well defined because $(-1)^2=(q-1)(-1)+q$). Then $\rho_-(\theta(x_{(m)}))=\sum_{w\in S_m}q^{\ell(w)}$ and $\rho_-(y_{(m)})=\sum_{w\in S_m}q^{-\ell(w)}$, so $c=\prod_{k=1}^m\frac{1+q+\cdots+q^{k-1}}{1+q^{-1}+\cdots+q^{-(k-1)}}=q^{\binom m2}$. Both sides of $\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda$ now hold in $H_K$; as they are elements of the free $A$-submodule $H_A$ and $H_A\hookrightarrow H_K$, they hold over $A$, hence over every $R$ by the base change $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto q$. The companion identity follows by applying $\theta$ again. At $q=1$ the formula reads $\theta(T_w)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}$, the pullback along the sign automorphism. Sources: Mathas, manuscript, Notes on Chapter 3, Notes 3 and 4 (printed pp. 34--35), which record the $\#$ automorphism and $m_\lambda^\#=q^an_\lambda$ and cite Murphy's proof; that citation is not used here, the argument above is the replacement, with Hoefsmit's Corollary 3.20 supplying the split semisimplicity. KMR, (3.14) and §8 (Theorem 8.5), contain the parallel sign automorphism and its role in the signed-conjugate comparison, read as an analogue. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The permutation form is H-contravariant and restricts to the DJ form
items.statement:
In the notation of [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], for every commutative $R$ and $q\in R^\times$, the permutation form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ is well defined, symmetric and $R$-bilinear, with $\beta(x_\lambda T_d,x_\lambda T_e)=\delta_{d,e}q^{\ell(d)}$ on the distinguished basis of [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]]. It is $H$-contravariant:
$$\beta(xh,y)=\beta(x,yh^*)\qquad(x,y\in M(\lambda),\ h\in H).$$
Its restriction $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ to the polytabloid module $P(\lambda)$ satisfies the same identity for $x,y\in P(\lambda)$ and is called the DJ form. Both $\beta$ and $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ are compatible with every base change $R\to R'$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Well-definedness, symmetry and bilinearity are immediate from the freeness of the distinguished basis [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]](1). By additivity in $x$ and $y$ it suffices to verify contravariance for $x=x_\lambda T_d$, $y=x_\lambda T_e$ and $h=T_i$ (generators), and the identity extends to words by induction. Writing $t=t^\lambda\cdot d$, $u=t^\lambda\cdot e$, one distinguishes the three positions of the pair $(i,i+1)$ in $t$ and in $u$, using the action rules of [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]](3) on the left and on the right. In each of the resulting cases the same-row/same-column and length-change conditions for $t$ and $u$ are linked by the relations $d'=e\Leftrightarrow d=e'$ and $d\,s_i=e$, and one checks term by term that the two sides either both vanish or that the $q$ and $(q-1)$ coefficients combine; for example, when $t\cdot s_i$ is row standard with $\ell(d')>\ell(d)$ and $u\cdot s_i$ is row standard with $\ell(e')<\ell(e)$, the identity reduces to $\delta_{d',e}q^{\ell(d')}=q\delta_{d,e'}q^{\ell(d)}+(q-1)\delta_{d,e}q^{\ell(d)}$, and the incompatible subcase analysis leaves only the two mutually exclusive configurations in which both sides vanish, while when $u\cdot s_i$ is not row standard or $u\cdot s_i$ is standard with the same length direction, the two sides are visibly equal. This is the standard verification that the q-permutation form is contravariant; the same case split is what underlies the classical tabloid form of [[def-integral-tabloid-bilinear-form-and-specht-gram-matrix]] at $q=1$. The restriction statement is by definition of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$; base change is immediate from the formula. No step assumes that $\beta$ or its restriction is nondegenerate. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Murphy cellular basis, the cell law and the Murphy form
items.statement:
For every commutative $R$, $q\in R^\times$, and $\lambda\vdash n$ with its row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an $R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.
2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and $I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$ (dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.
3. The **Murphy cell module** $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.
4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with $m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is symmetric, associative in the sense $G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.
5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every base change.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank $f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|=\dim S^\lambda_{\mathbb Q(q)}$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: This is the integral Murphy theory, assembled from the two independent treatments read for this page. Mathas, manuscript, §3: Lemma 3.2 and Proposition 3.3 (row-coset bookkeeping), Lemma 3.12 (the Garnir relation $m_{t^\lambda g}=\sum_{\tau\rhd g}m_{t^\lambda\tau}+h$ with $h$ in higher-shape row-standard spans), Lemma 3.14 (straightening of $m_{st}$ in terms of standard tableaux and higher shapes), Corollary 3.15 (the fixed-first-index multiplication rule modulo the higher ideal), Theorem 3.18 (Murphy Basis Theorem; the basis statement is assembled on printed p. 23 from the Garnir straightening plus the RSK rank count $\sum_\lambda(f^\lambda)^2=n!$, and item (ii) there is the cell law), with Corollary 3.17 for the two-sidedness of the ideals. The general cellular-language assertions, the form $G_\lambda$, its symmetry, associativity and the radical being a submodule, are the Graham-Lehrer theory as recalled in Chapter 2 of the manuscript (Proposition 2.7 for the symmetry and associativity of the cell form and for the radical being a submodule), instantiated at this basis; the form is concretely the coefficient of $x_\lambda$ in $x_\lambda T_{d(s)}T_{d(t)^{-1}}x_\lambda$ expanded in the standard basis, as in Ryom-Hansen, arXiv:0904.4243v5, §2 (PDF p. 6) (where $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, the standard elements $x_{st}$, the dominance ideals $N^\lambda$, the module $S^A_q(\lambda)$, the action rules (6) and the Garnir relations (9) are stated in the same normalization). Everything is defined over $A=\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$ and the basis statements hold after every base change; \emph{no generic semisimplicity, no division by quantum factorials and no rank count over $\mathbb Q$ is used for the integral assertions}, which come from the integral straightening. The higher ideals are two-sided because of the star symmetry and the straightening; this is Corollary 3.17 of the manuscript. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Integral polytabloid straightening for the comparison
items.strategy:
BUILD TARGET; the Murphy half is discharged by [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]], which is complete against the read sources (Mathas §3, Ryom-Hansen §2). The polytabloid half has no complete proof in the sources read for this batch, so this item is an owner escalation; the exact state of the evidence is as follows.

What is established: the definition of $P(\lambda)$ and the row-module structure (this page, items 1-2); the historical theorem that $\{z_\lambda T_\tau:\tau\in D^{st}_{\lambda^{\mathsf T}}\}$ is a basis of $z_\lambda H$ is Dipper-James, Proc. LMS 52 (1986), Theorem 5.6, as quoted in Heard-Kujawa, arXiv:2207.00654, §2.5 (their (2.5.1) with the same generator $z_\lambda$ and the same right-module conventions); the full text of Dipper-James 1986 is closed (Wiley returns 403; see the coverage record and batch notes for the attempts).

What is available as a complete analogue: KMR, Universal graded Specht modules for cyclotomic Hecke algebras, defines the universal (column) Specht module by its own generators and relations, proves a spanning set by a Garnir straightening over an arbitrary commutative ground ring (Proposition 7.14), identifies it with the Hecke graded column Specht module over a field (Theorem 7.19, using Brundan-Kleshchev and Hu-Mathas), and obtains the standard basis over any integral domain (Corollary 7.20) and its presentation by the relations (Corollary 7.22). The precise missing input for this item is therefore the identification, over a general commutative ring with a unit parameter, of the universal column Specht module with the ordinary Dipper-James polytabloid module $P(\lambda)$ of this page, or equivalently an integral proof of the standard-q-polytabloid straightening with the exact Garnir coefficients; the historical proof of both is exactly Theorem 5.6 of Dipper-James 1986 (and Murphy 1995 for the comparison). The recommended routes are recorded in the batch notes: (A) a local proof by the q-analogue of the classical James/Dipper-James Garnir argument, for which the accessible complete template is the Murphy-side proof in Mathas §3 (the argument structure, coset factorisations and leading-unit triangularity are the same) and the q=1 case in James SLN 682; or (B) an owner decision to install the KLR/graded prerequisite chain in a separate pair. No incomplete step is presented as complete, and no unnamed scalar, no vanishing scalar and no source-20 Murphy prototype is assumed. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Theta transports the Murphy cellular structure to the signed cell modules
items.statement:
Let $\theta$ be the involutive automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $m_{st}$, $I^{\rhd\lambda}$, $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$, $G_\lambda$ be as in [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]]. Then:

1. $\theta(m_{st})=\theta(T_{d(s)}^*)\theta(m_\lambda)\theta(T_{d(t)})$ with $\theta(m_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda$; $\{\theta(m_{st}):s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is again an $R$-basis of $H$; the spans $\theta(I^{\rhd\lambda})$ and $\theta(I^{\unrhd\lambda})$ of the $\theta$-images of the corresponding basis elements are two-sided ideals of $H$ (images of two-sided ideals under the automorphism $\theta$), and $(\{\theta(m_{st})\},\unrhd)$ is again a cellular basis with the same dominance poset, whose ideal filtration is the $\theta$-image of the original one. The image ideals are in general \emph{different} subspaces from the originals: already for $n=2$, $\lambda=(2)$ one has $\theta(x_{(2)})=q-T_1\notin R(1+T_1)=I^{\unrhd(2)}$. The poset is preserved; the ideal subspaces are not, in general.
2. $\theta$ induces an isomorphism of right $H$-modules $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)^\theta\xrightarrow{\sim}\theta(M(\lambda))/(\theta(M(\lambda))\cap\theta(I^{\rhd\lambda}))$, $m_t\mapsto\theta(m_t)$, whose target is the cell module of the transported basis; in particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)^\theta$ is free of rank $f^\lambda$ with basis $\{\theta(m_t):t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.
3. The transported form $G_\lambda^\theta(x,y):=G_\lambda(\theta^{-1}x,\theta^{-1}y)$ is the Murphy form of the transported basis; it is symmetric, is associative for the twisted action $G_\lambda^\theta(x\cdot h,y)=G_\lambda^\theta(x,y\cdot h^*)$ and has the same radical, so the assignment $x\mapsto\theta^{-1}x$ identifies the twisted cell module with the cell module for the same underlying $H$-form.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ is free of rank $f^{\lambda'}=f^\lambda$ and carries the transported form $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: An algebra automorphism that commutes with the cellular anti-involution transports a cell datum to a cell datum with the same poset: axioms (i) and (ii) of a cell datum are transported by $\theta$, and the triangular axiom (iii) is transported because the images $\theta(I^{\rhd\lambda})$, $\theta(I^{\unrhd\lambda})$ of two-sided ideals under the algebra automorphism $\theta$ are again two-sided ideals, and they are exactly the spans of the transported basis elements $\theta(m_{uv})$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$, respectively $\mu\unrhd\lambda$, because $\theta$ is $R$-linear. Axiom (i) holds because $\theta(m_{st})^*=\theta(m_{st}^*)=\theta(m_{ts})$, and axiom (ii) is obtained by applying the original cell law to $m_{st}\theta^{-1}(h)$ and then $\theta$. \emph{Warning:} $\theta$ does not preserve the ideals as subspaces in general --- already for $n=2$, $\lambda=(2)$ one has $\theta(x_{(2)})=q-T_1\notin R(1+T_1)=I^{\unrhd(2)}$ --- so the transported cell datum must be used with its own ideal filtration, and comparisons with the original filtration have to go through the sign twist. This is the statement class of Mathas, manuscript, Notes on Chapter 3, Notes 3 and 4 (printed pp. 34--35), which record the $\#$ automorphism and that the $\#$ -transported basis $N=\{n_{st}\}$ is again a cellular basis; the argument above is self-contained and does not use the Murphy Theorem 5.2 cited there. The displayed formula for $\theta(m_{st})$ is the direct expansion of $\theta$ on the product $m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$: it uses $\theta(T_{d(s)}^*)=\theta(T_{d(s)})^*$ and $\theta(m_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda$ from [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]](1) and (4); the unit factors produced by $\theta(T_{d(s)})$ and $\theta(T_{d(t)})$ are carried along, and the basis claim needs no coefficient comparison because $\theta$ is an invertible $R$-linear map. The map $m_t\mapsto\theta(m_t)$ is induced by $\theta$ on $M(\lambda)$, since $\theta(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})=\theta(M(\lambda))\cap\theta(I^{\rhd\lambda})$; injectivity and surjectivity are those of $\theta$ on the ambient free modules, and the basis statement follows from item (1). For (3), the transported form is well defined on the transported basis, and associativity reads $G_\lambda(\theta^{-1}(x\theta(h)),\theta^{-1}y)=G_\lambda(\theta^{-1}x,\theta^{-1}(y\theta(h)^*))$, which is the associativity of $G_\lambda$ because $\theta^{-1}(x\theta(h))=\theta^{-1}(x)\theta^{-1}(\theta(h))=\theta^{-1}(x)h$ and $\theta^{-1}(y\theta(h)^*)=\theta^{-1}(y)\theta^{-1}(\theta(h)^*)=\theta^{-1}(y)h^*$ with $\theta$ commuting with $*$. The radical assertion is the subspace statement $\mathrm{rad}(G_\lambda^\theta)=\theta(\mathrm{rad}\,G_\lambda)$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Murphy cells are the same-shape contragredient Specht duals
items.statement: For every commutative $R$, unit $q$ and partition $\lambda$ there is an explicit perfect $R$-bilinear star-balanced pairing $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$, giving $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\cong P(\lambda)^\circ$ naturally under all coefficient-ring base changes. Equivalently, the kernel of the row-permutation quotient onto $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is the orthogonal complement of $P(\lambda)$ for the independently defined permutation form, and its preimage in $M(\lambda)$ is $M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$. The pairing matrix on the actual standard bases has determinant a unit in $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$; its entries and inverse are given by finite tableau formulas. No nondegeneracy of the form restricted to $P(\lambda)$ is required. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: BUILD TARGET; owner escalation, no complete proof in the sources read. The statement is the ordinary Hecke form of the classical relation between the Murphy cell module and the Dipper-James polytabloid module. The sources that state it defer the proof: Mathas, manuscript, Warning following the definition of the Specht module after Corollary 3.19 (printed p. 25) says the cell module of shape $\lambda$ is isomorphic to the dual of the Dipper-James module indexed by the conjugate partition and refers the reader to the original papers; Kleshchev, arXiv:0909.4844v1, Remark 5.5, records the same relation at the level of simple modules (dual to the older literature; $D_\mu\cong D(\mu^t)\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$). The precise missing input is the integral standard-basis and Garnir theory of $P(\lambda)$, i.e. [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]], together with its unit-determinant pairing with the Murphy basis; both belong to Theorem 5.6 of Dipper-James 1986 and Murphy 1995, whose full texts are closed. A complete accessible analogue of the whole statement exists in the universal graded setting: KMR, Theorem 7.25, proves the graded contragredient duality $S_\mu(O)\cong S^\mu(O)^{\sim}\langle\mathrm{def}_\Lambda\rangle$ over every integral domain $O$ by an explicit triangular-form argument, and Theorem 7.19 identifies the universal modules with the Hecke graded column/row Specht modules over a field. The exact remaining gap, the recommended remediation routes and the acquisition history are recorded in the batch notes. Because [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]] is escalated, this theorem is escalated as a consumer as well. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Ordinary Specht modules and forms match signed conjugate Murphy cells
items.statement:
For every commutative $R$, unit $q$ and partition $\lambda$, there is a base-change compatible isomorphism
$$\Phi_\lambda:P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$$
of right $H$-modules, and an explicit unit $u_\lambda(q)\in A^\times$ (a monomial in $q$) such that
$$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$
with $G_{\lambda'}$ the Murphy form of [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and $\theta$ the sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. The unit $u_\lambda$ is computed in the fixed generator and form normalizations of this page; no unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar is permitted. Consequently the form radicals and their quotients correspond after every field specialization: $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all Jantzen divisibility submodules and reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and $\theta$, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: BUILD TARGET; owner escalation, no complete proof in the sources read. This is Murphy's Lemma/Theorem 5.2 of the 1995 J. Algebra paper, stated there in the form of an isomorphism between the ordinary Dipper-James Specht module and the signed conjugate of the Murphy cell module of the conjugate partition, with the unit computed from the two normalizations; Mathas's Warning (manuscript, printed p. 25) and Note 3 (printed p. 34) record the two missing twist ingredients (the dual/conjugate dictionary and the sign automorphism $\#$), and both refer to Murphy's proof rather than reproducing it. The full text of Murphy 1995 is closed (Elsevier 401/403; the actual attempts and their outcomes are recorded in the batch notes and in the historical attempt file). The accessible complete analogue is KMR, §8, Theorem 8.5 (with Lemma 8.4): over an arbitrary commutative unital ground ring $O$, the universal Specht module labelled by $\mu$ is isomorphic to the sgn-twist of the universal Specht module labelled by the conjugate $\mu'$, and vice versa, proved by the generator-and-relations method: the conjugate generator is shown to satisfy the defining relations (idempotent, $y_r$, $\psi_r$ and Garnir) of the other side, using Lemma 8.4 for degrees and the correspondence of Garnir nodes and bricks. To apply that method here one needs the analogous classical presentations of $P(\lambda)$ and $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ over arbitrary commutative rings; the row/Murphy side is available ([[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]], [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]), the column side is the escalated item [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]. The unit $u_\lambda$ must be computed on the two explicit generators, $\Phi_\lambda z_\lambda=\theta(m_{t^{\lambda'}})$ up to the unit already present in $\theta(m_{\lambda'})=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))}y_{\lambda'}$, and is not guessed. Because the two prerequisite items are escalated, this theorem is escalated; the precise gap and the remediation routes are recorded in the batch notes. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Polytabloid specialization and the exact signed multiplicity dictionary
items.statement: Assume the isomorphism and unit identity of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. For every field $F$ at $q=1$, $P(\lambda)$ specializes to the ordinary integral-polytabloid Specht module $F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ of [[def-integral-specht-lattice-and-base-change]], with its standard form, and $\theta$ becomes tensoring with the sign representation; this specialization is compatible with [[lem-conjugate-specht-sign-duality-over-fields]]. For an arbitrary unit $q$ over a field, $[P(\lambda):D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'):D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}]$ whenever $D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}\ne0$, and the simultaneous $q$-twist is the same $\theta$ on both sides. For a Schur corner already proved to send the Weyl module $W(\lambda)$ to $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ and its head $L(\lambda)$ to $D^{\mu}_{\mathrm M}$, the ordinary dictionary is $F(W(\lambda'))\cong P(\lambda)^\theta$ and $F(L(\lambda'))\cong(D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta$, including zero; it is never the untwisted conjugate-dual identity. No Schur-algebra or source-20 convention result is a prerequisite of this conditional dictionary. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Conditional corollary: its proof composes the escalated theorem [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]] with published q=1 facts, so it is escalated as a consumer. The q=1 specialization clause, once the theorem is available: at $q=1$ the Hecke algebra is $\mathbb C[S_n]$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]), the elements $x_\lambda,y_{\lambda'}$ become the row sum and the column antisymmetrizer, so $z_\lambda$ becomes the integral polytabloid generator and $P(\lambda)_{q=1}$ is the ordinary integral-polytabloid Specht lattice of [[def-integral-specht-lattice-and-base-change]]; $\theta$ at $q=1$ acts as $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$, so the theorem reads $S^\lambda\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\cong(S^{\lambda'})^*$, which is the published [[lem-conjugate-specht-sign-duality-over-fields]]; unwinding the comparison in the other order gives the dictionary. The multiplicity clause is formal from exactness and simplicity preservation of $(-)^\theta$ ([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]])(2). The Schur-corner clause is a conditional application only: it quantifies over corners already proved to carry the stated functoriality and is not a backward dependency on any Schur-algebra or source-20 result. The precise state of the gap is recorded in the batch notes; no invented unit and no unconditional Schur identity is asserted. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Untwisted conjugation changes the module
items.statement: Over $\mathbb Q$ at $q=1$ and $n=3$, the Murphy cell module $C_{\mathrm M}((1,1,1))$ is the sign module with $T_i=-1$, while the ordinary polytabloid module $P((3))$ and its dual are the trivial module with $T_i=1$. Hence $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ}$ without the twist $\theta$ is false in general; the correct statement is $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with $\theta$ the sign automorphism. This reproduces the actual source-20 root countermodel using only the new foundations of this pair. No choice principle is used.
